headline: Highest risk is medium: social-auto-upload can exfiltrate account/media data over broad egress, while awesome-python is non-runnable and adds no direct interaction surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. agent_a is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while agent_b has no filesystem read, no MCP, and no browser parsing surface that would ingest agent_a outputs by default.
conditions: IF agent_a becomes runnable and its outputs are copied into agent_b inputs, injection risk appears.
IF a shared clipboard or shared workspace is introduced, agent_b could parse attacker-controlled text.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected; do not copy agent_a output into agent_b.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared workspace between the agents.
Require manual review of any text passed from agent_a to agent_b.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b touches account data and media and has broad network egress, so it can transmit sensitive content; agent_a is docs-only and non-runnable, so it does not add a second leak path. The pair still creates a default leakage risk if agent_b processes user media or account state and uploads it.
conditions: IF agent_b is given account data or private media, it can send that data over network egress.
IF agent_b is connected to any shared workspace containing sensitive files, those files may be exposed.
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive test accounts.
Block outbound network access except to approved upload endpoints.
Separate sensitive media from the agent_b workspace.
Review account permissions before each run.
requires-engineering: add per-file allowlists for uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. agent_a has no write, network, or filesystem permissions shown, and agent_b explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Without shared mutable resources, capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF agent_a is later given write access to the same directory as agent_b, conflict risk appears.
IF either agent gains git-write or filesystem-write permissions, re-evaluate for contention.
mitigations: Keep agent_a read-only.
Do not grant agent_b filesystem write or git write.
Run each agent in separate directories.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles for any future shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can act on uploaded media/account data, but agent_a produces no outputs or facts because it is non-runnable. That makes a cascade from agent_a into agent_b unlikely; the remaining risk is ordinary operator error when feeding content into agent_b.
conditions: IF operator-supplied text from agent_a is manually pasted into agent_b workflows, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF agent_b is configured to auto-post without review, erroneous uploads can cascade.
mitigations: Do not use agent_a as an upstream content source.
Require human review before any upload by agent_b.
Use a staging account for uploads.
Pause automation for first-run validation.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before posting.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b handles account data and media and uploads via external APIs, so residency and retention obligations may apply; agent_a is docs-only and not a compliance-bearing runtime. The pair’s compliance risk is driven by agent_b’s external transmission, with no documented controls showing residency or retention alignment.
conditions: IF regulated or personal media is uploaded through agent_b, external processing obligations apply.
IF retention or deletion requirements exist for the account data, agent_b must honor them.
mitigations: Use only non-regulated test content.
Confirm the destination service’s retention policy before upload.
Document a deletion workflow for uploaded media.
Limit uploads to accounts covered by existing consent.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
